newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish finmin says '98 spending to focus on flood.
newsitem.headline: Polish finmin says '98 spending to focus on flood.

text.p: Polish Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Wednesday reconstruction of areas devastated by July's flood will be his 1998 budget draft's priority and spending in other areas will be cut.

Belka said the flooding, which hit Poland more than three weeks ago causing billions of dollars in damage, had forced him to trim his earlier tentative spending proposals because he did not want to abandon the bill's macroeconomic targets.

He reaffirmed he would not drop his plan to cut the budget deficit next year to 1.9 percent of gross domestic product from 1997's planned 2.8 percent and curb year-on-year inflation to less than 10 percent from June's 15.3 percent.
"This will be a budget of modest spending in many areas...and wage increases will be limited next year," Belka told a news conference.

International financial organisations and the central bank have urged the government to propose an even smaller budget deficit to curb domestic demand, which may hit the economy if its growth continues.
Belka said it was too early to give more details before cabinet debates on the budget draft, due later in the month and in September.
Before the flood, Belka had planned to offer significant spending increases for internal security, health and education.
Belka's proposals, if they are pushed through the current government, can be modified by the next parliament that will emerge from elections on September 21.
